problems.title: Three angles do not determine a unique pair
problems.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Three of the eight angles sum to 198°. Find the angles.
problems.idea: All eight angles have one of two supplementary measures.
formulas: The two measures are t and 180°-t.
steps: If the selected three are equal, 3t=198° gives t=66°, so the pair is 66°,114°.
If two have measure t and one is its supplement, 2t+(180°-t)=198° gives t=18°, so the pair is 18°,162°.
Both selections can be made among the eight angles.
problems.note: The wording does not say which three angles are selected, so a unique answer needs an extra condition.

problems.title: Successive percentage changes
problems.question: A price is halved twice and then increased by 20% twice. What is the overall percentage change?
formulas: New price=old price·(1+r) for an increase r; use 1-r for a decrease.
steps: Halving twice leaves 0.5·0.5=0.25 of the original price.
The increases multiply this by 1.2²=1.44.
The final fraction is 0.25·1.44=0.36, meaning a decrease of 1-0.36=0.64.

problems.title: Put linked ratios on the same scale
problems.question: Four numbers sum to 64. Their consecutive ratios are 5:6,2:3,3:4. Find them.
problems.idea: Match the middle numbers in each pair of ratios.
formulas: Equivalent ratios are obtained by multiplying every part by the same number.
steps: From a:b=5:6 and b:c=2:3, choose a:b:c=5:6:9.
Since c:d=3:4, extend this to 5:6:9:12.
The ratio parts sum to 32; the scale factor is 64/32=2.

problems.title: Work outward through nested absolute values
problems.question: Evaluate $(2.5-3\frac13)\,|-1-|-2-|-3|||\div(\frac13-2)$.
problems.idea: Start with the innermost absolute value.
formulas: $|u|$ is the nonnegative distance of u from zero.
steps: The first factor is 5/2-10/3=-5/6, so the numerator is -5.
The divisor is 1/3-2=-5/3; dividing gives (-5)/(-5/3)=3.

problems.title: An integer passenger count
problems.question: A bus has fewer than 100 passengers. There are twice as many seated as standing. At a stop 4% leave. How many remain?
problems.idea: The original count is divisible by both 3 and 25.
formulas: If 4% of N is an integer, then N/25 is an integer.
steps: The seating ratio 2:1 makes N a multiple of 3.
Since a whole number of passengers leave, N must also be a multiple of 25.
The only positive common multiple below 100 is 75. Three leave, so 72 remain.

problems.title: Compare two angle bisectors
problems.question: K lies inside angle ABC=40°. KA is perpendicular to BA, and KC is parallel to BA, meeting the corresponding sides at A and C. Find the acute angle between the bisector lines of ABC and AKC.
problems.idea: Measure both bisector lines against the direction BA.
formulas: A right angle has a 45° bisector; a 40° angle has a 20° bisector.
steps: Draw BA horizontally rightward and BC 40° above it.
From interior K, KA points down to BA and KC points left to BC, making AKC=90°.
The line of its bisector makes an acute 45° angle with BA. The ABC bisector makes 20°.
The acute difference is 45°-20°=25°.

problems.title: Compare transport work
problems.question: Three trucks move 800 tonnes through 24 km in 2 hours. How long do four identical trucks need for 600 tonnes through 30 km?
problems.idea: Under the standard work model, time is proportional to tonnes times distance and inversely proportional to truck count.
steps: The transport-work ratio is (600·30)/(800·24)=15/16.
Four trucks instead of three multiply the time by 3/4.
This is 1 hour,24 minutes,22.5 seconds.
problems.note: This uses equal, constant transport productivity per truck and the usual tonne-kilometre model.

problems.title: Turn percentages of angles into a ratio
problems.question: One triangle angle is 20% of the second and 25% of the third. Find all three.
problems.idea: Use the smallest angle as one ratio unit.
steps: Let the smallest angle be x. The second is 5x and the third 4x.
Their sum is 10x=180°, so x=18°.
The other angles are 90° and 72°.

problems.title: A bisector between two parallel lines
problems.question: In the source diagram AB∥CE, angle ABK=40° and KDC=80°. Find the acute angle between the bisector of BKD and CE.
problems.idea: Use the parallel horizontal lines to measure both rays from K.
formulas: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal; a bisector halves an angle.
steps: Ray KB is 40° above the rightward horizontal. Ray KD is 80° below it.
Its bisector is 60° below KB, or 20° below the horizontal.

problems.title: Deleting an endpoint gives two answers
problems.question: Erase one integer from 1,2,...,40 so that one of the remaining integers equals the mean of the other 38. Which number can be erased?
problems.idea: If the remaining special number is k, the sum of all 39 remaining numbers must be 39k.
steps: The original sum is 40·41/2=820. If r is erased, 820-r=39k.
For 1≤r≤40, the integer k can only be 20 or 21.
For k=20, r=40; for k=21, r=1.
Each works: the other 38 numbers then have sum 38k.
problems.note: Both endpoints satisfy the printed condition; it does not determine a unique erased number.
